reference_observations.description: Four Darwin questions occur in the body; Smith’s interlined answers are literally preserved in footnotes 3–6. They are attributed historical answers, not editorial paraphrase and not Darwin target voice. Questions, answers and chapter use require separate dates.

One query survives through Stokes’s 1846 publication; the remainder of the original question list is lost. Raw after-May-31, 1837 bounds and uncertain exact date remain, while publication establishes this wording before the current period.

The rewritten ant-plant memorandum was reportedly sent today but is not preserved inline; its 1908 publication is not automatically the identical manuscript. Missing opening and excised lines remain gaps.
Bentham’s full 17 blocks include selection counterarguments, doubts about Buckman controls, and distinct Herbin/Sonnini quotations. They do not establish acceptance of pangenesis.

relationship_details.rationale: Explicit letter of the 3rd and enclosed leaked note identify antecedent. Weekday/day conflict affects precise dating, not relationship.
Just received Grey note returning own 940, copies forwarded to Stokes; corroborated explicit May10 acknowledgement 1021.
1017 request followed by 1019 dated-response; 1021 explicitly encloses that letter and answer. This establishes receipt by November10 without choosing between contradictory November6/Saturday dating.

corrections.description: P4 contains the heading Second; P5 is the second question. There is no missing second-question wording. The claims are in Pusey’s added published notes, not the delivered sermon body; Darwin’s scoring is not agreement or permission to publish.

The worker still calls November 6 exact. The autograph also says Saturday, while November 6, 1846 was Friday. Keep the exact-day conflict and prior November 10 forwarding bound; do not choose November 7.

Circa November 26 is an inferred earliest Thursday, not a secure point date. Stokes 1019 did not know the printer mechanism, so it cannot be the complete prompt for this later acceptance of an explanation.
January 2 has a supplied 1847 year. Both volumes arrived yesterday, January 1 under that year; receipt is not full reading and the planned visit is not confirmed attendance.
All eight inline figures concern echinoderms. The mentioned fish sketch is not thereby preserved; retain the long separate enclosure and annotations, and uncertain young-fish length rendering.

summary: Ten targets and four contexts reuse matched accepted primary readings. A fresh full reread of Ridley 11765 corrects the worker’s invented missing second question. No new current-period edges. Smith 2235A is an 1858 mixed-questionnaire lead; Stokes earlier relationships remain unchanged. Original date qualifiers, missing sources, complete enclosures and eight Agassiz figures are retained.
